title: Validation of a machine learning algorithm for early severe sepsis prediction: a retrospective study predicting severe sepsis up to 48 h in advance using a diverse dataset from 461 US hospitals
summary: A machine-learning algorithm predicted severe-sepsis onset from retrospective records across 461 health centers, reporting AUROC 0.827 at 48 hours before onset and external-dataset AUROC 0.752 at that horizon. This is retrospective validation; prospective clinical impact was not tested.
ai_technology: A machine-learning algorithm predicts severe-sepsis onset from electronic health-record variables up to 48 hours ahead.
organization: Cabell Huntington Hospital, Huntington, WV, USA

evidence.tested: A 461-hospital retrospective cohort evaluates early machine-learning prediction of severe sepsis. Interpretation is limited to the source's cohort, data or test setting.
evidence.unknown: The paper reports the relevant cohort/image/field dataset, comparator or reference, and validation/test evaluation; the judgment does not imply prospective clinical benefit.
evidence.ai_role: A machine-learning algorithm predicts severe-sepsis onset from electronic health-record variables up to 48 hours ahead.

source_review.scope: Primary result-bearing material for the stated method, result and evaluation, with bibliographic version information.
